description: Kubernetes core decomposed. Apiserver + etcd + scheduler + controller-manager + kubelet + kube-proxy. Pod lifecycle, init containers, sidecar containers, probes, resource requests/limits, QoS classes, scheduling decisions, preemption.

sub_mechanisms.name: kube_apiserver
sub_mechanisms.definition: REST API serving cluster state. Auth + admission + storage in etcd.
sub_mechanisms.why: Single source of truth. All components read/write through apiserver. Highly available via multiple replicas with shared etcd.

sub_mechanisms.name: etcd_cluster_store
sub_mechanisms.definition: Raft-based distributed KV. Stores all K8s objects. Strong consistency.
sub_mechanisms.why: Cluster state. Performance critical: API responsiveness depends on etcd. 3-5 node cluster typical. Backups essential.

sub_mechanisms.name: kube_scheduler
sub_mechanisms.definition: Watches for unscheduled pods; assigns to nodes based on resources + constraints + scoring.
sub_mechanisms.why: Decoupled from creation: pod created, scheduler binds. Pluggable via scheduler plugins. Default has good behaviour for general workloads.

sub_mechanisms.name: kubelet
sub_mechanisms.definition: Per-node agent. Reads pod specs from apiserver; manages container lifecycle via CRI.
sub_mechanisms.why: Talks to apiserver + container runtime. Reports node + pod status. Critical: kubelet down → node effectively dead.

sub_mechanisms.name: kube_proxy
sub_mechanisms.definition: Implements Service networking via iptables or IPVS. Distributes traffic to pod endpoints.
sub_mechanisms.why: L4 service routing. iptables: many rules at scale; IPVS: scales better. Per-node component; not in path of every packet on modern CNIs (some use eBPF replacing).

sub_mechanisms.name: init_container
sub_mechanisms.definition: Runs to completion before app container starts. Sequential.
sub_mechanisms.why: Setup tasks: DB migrations, config download, dependency wait. Failures block pod start. Different image from main container.

sub_mechanisms.name: sidecar_container_native
sub_mechanisms.definition: K8s 1.29+: restartPolicy=Always init container. Runs alongside main container; main can terminate without waiting.
sub_mechanisms.why: Standardised sidecar lifecycle. Before 1.29: regular container; ordering issues on shutdown. Native sidecar fixes.

sub_mechanisms.name: resource_requests_limits
sub_mechanisms.definition: Requests: scheduler reservation. Limits: enforced cap. Memory limit hit = OOMKilled.
sub_mechanisms.why: Requests determine scheduling; limits prevent runaway. Set both. CPU limits controversial (throttle vs no limit + monitor).

sub_mechanisms.name: QoS_classes
sub_mechanisms.definition: BestEffort (no requests/limits), Burstable (requests but no limits, or limits > requests), Guaranteed (limits = requests).
sub_mechanisms.why: Eviction order under pressure: BestEffort first, Burstable next, Guaranteed last. Important to know for production.

sub_mechanisms.name: preemption
sub_mechanisms.definition: Higher-priority pods evict lower-priority to be scheduled.
sub_mechanisms.why: PriorityClass with high value. Critical workloads guaranteed scheduling. Lower-priority pods rescheduled or stay pending.

sub_mechanisms.name: taints_tolerations
sub_mechanisms.definition: Taint on node = repel pods. Toleration on pod = allowed to schedule despite taint.
sub_mechanisms.why: Reserve nodes (GPU, special hardware). Default master node taint. Dedicated nodes for specific workloads.

sub_mechanisms.name: node_affinity
sub_mechanisms.definition: Pod prefers/requires nodes with matching labels. requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution etc.
sub_mechanisms.why: Spread across AZs, prefer specific instance types, co-locate with specific workloads. Standard scheduling control.

derivation_rules.name: etcd_performance_caps_K8s_throughput
derivation_rules.why: Every K8s operation reads/writes etcd. Slow etcd = slow apiserver = slow everything. Tune: SSD, sufficient RAM, periodic compaction. Standard K8s operational concern.

derivation_rules.name: QoS_guaranteed_for_critical_workloads
if: workload must not be evicted under pressure
derivation_rules.why: BestEffort + Burstable evicted before Guaranteed. Critical databases, control planes → Guaranteed. Standard production pattern.

derivation_rules.name: memory_limit_OOMKills
if: pod uses more memory than limit
derivation_rules.why: Hard limit; no negotiation. Set conservatively + monitor. CPU limits throttle (slower); memory limits kill. Different fail modes.

derivation_rules.name: init_containers_for_dependencies
then: init container is the K8s idiom
derivation_rules.why: Doesn't bloat app image. Sequential: A → B → main. Failure = pod restart. Standard pattern for migrations, config fetch, wait-for-DB.

derivation_rules.name: scheduler_constraints_cascade
if: pod has resource requests + affinity + tolerations
then: available nodes = intersection of all constraints
derivation_rules.why: All constraints must satisfy. Over-constrained = pending pod. Common debug: 'why won't this schedule?'. Tools: kubectl describe pod shows scheduler events.
